source.title: Standardizing Your Training Process for Human Activity Recognition Models: A Comprehensive Review in the Tunable Factors
source.authors: Yiran Huang; Hai-Qiang Zhao; Ye-Xu Zhou; T. Riedel; Michael Beigl

record.tranche_reason: The study varies optimizer and batch size in controlled HAR experiments and measures validation performance, a different setting and metric from the claim versions’ image and language benchmarks.
record.gate_note: The paper also varies learning rate, weight decay, early stopping, and model selection. These results are recorded where they bear on V4 or V5; the combined training-recipe comparison does not isolate either version. Review statistics and cited prior-work results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own optimizer and batch-size comparisons on held-out wearable activity data, extending the generalization question to a new setting. Its batch-size experiment does not establish the fixed training budget required by V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors emphasize incomplete reporting of training procedures, demonstrate sensitivity to training choices, and report higher LOSO macro F1 for their combined procedure across five datasets and three architectures. The combined comparison does not isolate optimizer or batch-size effects.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies wearable human activity recognition, using control-variable comparisons and a combined training-recipe experiment rather than the image and language settings in the versions. Its batch-size comparison does not state a fixed epoch budget.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer, initial learning rate, weight decay, batch size, early-stopping criterion, and model-selection criterion affect reported training or validation outcomes. The paper states the optimizer comparison is sensitive to hyperparameters and initialization.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Mobile and Ubiquitous Systems: Networking and Services
record.problems: The optimizer and batch-size comparison results are presented as curves without numerical values in the supplied text. The optimizer result is qualified by hyperparameter sensitivity and inappropriate initialization; batch-size values are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 compares combined training procedures and does not isolate optimizer or batch-size effects, so it was not used for V4 or V5 rows. Figure 3(b)–(c) and Figure 4 concern learning rate, weight decay, and early stopping rather than the tested versions; they are described in gate_note only insofar as relevant to the study’s training-factor scope.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label generalization, and chance-level held-out performance with random labels.
Width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity or initialization.

Image and language benchmarks; optimizer-specific learning-rate and schedule tuning; comparable training performance; momentum SGD; broader tuning; decoupled weight decay; optimizer switching; word-level language models.
Equal realized epoch budgets, a workload-dependent batch-size threshold, image and language workloads, and isolated tests of remedies such as longer training or warmup.
Dropout effects and interactions with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removal of highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No V5 verdict is justified without establishing equal epoch budgets. A shared maximum epoch count with early stopping is insufficient. Table 3 is already declared omitted and changes several training choices together.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Network width beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Image-classification and language benchmarks; broad optimizer tuning; momentum SGD; decoupled weight decay; switching optimizers; word-level language models.
Large-batch workloads in image classification and language modeling; fixed epoch budgets; adaptation by longer training, warmup, normalization, or regularization.
Dropout in fully connected or convolutional classifiers and its interaction with data augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: CNNLSTM
rows.operation_detail: Compared sGD, Adagrad, and Adam optimizer settings in the control-variates experiment.
rows.measure: Validation loss during training; authors state Adam yielded the best performance and sGD did not converge.
rows.note: The text reports Adam as best among the three and says sGD did not converge due to hyperparameter sensitivity and inappropriate initialization.
rows.check: Adam has the best reported validation performance, but SGD does not converge. The comparison uses the baseline Adam-oriented recipe without reported optimizer-specific tuning, so it does not establish an advantage between comparably optimized models. Results are stated qualitatively; numerical losses are unavailable.

rows.subject: CNNLSTM
rows.operation_detail: Compared different batch sizes in the control-variates experiment.

conditions.value: different sizes; specific values not stated

rows.measure: Validation loss during training; authors state smaller batch size led to better generalization.
rows.note: The text describes better generalization with smaller batch size; specific batch sizes and numerical losses are not stated.
rows.check: The authors explicitly report better generalization with smaller batches, but the common 60-epoch maximum includes validation-loss early stopping with 10-epoch patience. Equal realized epoch budgets are not established, so the result cannot establish V5's fixed-budget effect. Batch sizes and numerical losses cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.

relationships.condition: CNNLSTM on HAPT under the shared baseline training recipe
relationships.reason: R1 reports Adam performing best while SGD fails to converge, showing an adaptive-optimizer advantage in this setting; optimizer-specific tuning and comparable training performance are not established.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly performed best while SGD failed to converge, but the comparison remains unverified and comparable tuning was unestablished.
